content: A kick chart is a tool, often in the form of a graph or chart, used by pregnant women during the later stages of pregnancy to monitor and record the movements of their fetus. If the fetus does not move or kick a sufficient number of times within a specified time frame, typically 12 hours, it may indicate a potential problem with the pregnancy. However, the use of kick charts has declined over time. This is because many women often forget to complete them, and fetal movement patterns can vary significantly, which can lead to unnecessary anxiety or concern. In recent years, there has been a shift towards using pregnancy bracelets as a wearable alternative to traditional kick charts. These bracelets function as fetal kick counters. In the United Kingdom, midwives frequently ask pregnant women how many times their baby has moved or kicked in the past 12 hours. This is considered one of the best indicators of fetal health starting from the second trimester. It is generally expected that the fetus should move or kick at least ten times within any given 12-hour period. The pregnancy bracelets operate on a similar principle to kick charts. When the baby kicks, the mother moves a marker on the bracelet to record the movement. This method is considered more practical and convenient compared to using pen and paper. Currently, the two most widely promoted pregnancy bracelets are in the process of undergoing patent applications.
